findings.reason: define the scan-eligibility/stranded predicate once beside the path scan claim in imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py and have both the claim and the reset render that one definition, per the "one renderer, do not spell the clause inline" rule the section already applies to the prefix predicate.
findings.text: §14's `source_filter` bound on the `scanned` path spec is the negation of a path scan-eligibility predicate that already appears inline at imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:273, :309, :492, :605 and :218–220 and imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py:408 (all spelling `p.status = $discovered/$scanned AND p.triage_composite IS NULL`), while the plan writes its complement `n.status = 'discovered' AND n.triage_composite IS NOT NULL` in a different module; the reset therefore defines the stranded-row set with no shared owner with the scan claim that creates those rows, so a later edit to the claim's eligibility silently changes what the reset can recover

duplicate_owner-1.reason: The create-only seed removed the only known cause of a discovered row carrying a triage score, so the stranded set the bound recovers is a fixed historical one (42 rows at JET, ITER and TCV) that does not move with the scan claim's eligibility. Consolidating the six inline scan-eligibility spellings in imas_codex/discovery/paths into one owner is a refactor of the path-claim module outside §14, not a precondition for this bound.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the three surface additions (the create-only option at graph/client.py:611, the planned `source_filter` on `ResetSpec`, and the clause+params helper) each sit over behaviour that already lives in the owner module; none introduces a family of shallow wrappers, and two of the three are single new keyword/optional-field arguments to an existing deep function.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the section's planned reset `source_filter` re-expresses, as its negation, the path scan-eligibility predicate that already has no single owner; the finding below is the census.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 adds no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and names what it retires (`seed_missing_roots`, `create_child_paths`, and their exports) and merges (one prefix renderer plus helper, one reset call site per command) in its own text.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the section extends the mechanisms it names: the prefix renderer `render_path_prefix_clause` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:268, the single owner already called by the five path claims at discovery/paths/parallel.py:484/540/597/715/795, the two code-scan claims at discovery/code/graph_ops.py:141/566, and the scoped reset at discovery/base/reset.py:98), `reset_to_status` (discovery/base/reset.py:59, which already carries `path_prefixes`), and `GraphClient.create_nodes`' create-only write (graph/client.py:611, already landed), and it cites the `ON CREATE SET` create-if-absent form the repo already uses rather than inventing one.
